metadata.title: GUI-0102: Pharmacovigilance system
metadata.legal_basis: Health Canada administrative guidance, GUI-0102. Legislation prevails; read with the overview, regulations chapter, glossary and references.
metadata.applicability: Manufacturers and market authorization holders with in-scope marketed human drugs. This is one chapter, not the entire guideline. Confirm exclusions and the source overview.

metadata_verification: Source-register metadata; dates and legal status require human verification.

candidates.statement: In a planned deviation, the departure should be documented, evaluated and approved before the change is implemented.
candidates.context: A deviation is a change or departure from the steps and/or instructions outlined in an approved written procedure. These can be planned or unplanned. In an unplanned deviation, the departure is unexpected and could suggest a systematic deficiency which needs to be resolved.

candidates.statement: In an unplanned deviation, the departure is unexpected and could suggest a systematic deficiency which needs to be resolved.
candidates.context: In a planned deviation, the departure should be documented, evaluated and approved before the change is implemented. A systematic deficiency is a fundamental inadequacy that exists within the processes or mechanisms of a pharmacovigilance system. It can arise from inadequate planning, design, or oversight of the system. This deficiency impacts the system’s ability to function effectively, consistently, and achieve its intended goal. It is widespread instead of isolated. A widespread incident is one that is part of a series or pattern of similar occurrences.

candidates.statement: Establish a change control system to allow ongoing process optimization and a continuing state of control. The department responsible for the change should document, evaluate the impact, and approve all changes, as well as identify the appropriate effective date. Any significant change that impacts compliance of your pharmacovigilance responsibilities may require re-validation or verification of systems or processes.

candidates.statement: There should be an assessment to determine if adequate validation has been completed on an electronic system used to capture, process, manage or archive pharmacovigilance activities. Adequacy should be assessed based on the criticality of the system and its intended use. Validation confirms that the system is reliable, credible and will perform as expected. You should document how validation, testing, and re-validation is to be conducted.
candidates.context: Validation of computerized systems Validation reports should be produced to document the results of the validation tests you performed. The results should clearly indicate that the system can be used as intended and is performing as specified.

candidates.statement: Validation reports should be produced to document the results of the validation tests you performed. The results should clearly indicate that the system can be used as intended and is performing as specified.
candidates.context: There should be an assessment to determine if adequate validation has been completed on an electronic system used to capture, process, manage or archive pharmacovigilance activities. Adequacy should be assessed based on the criticality of the system and its intended use. Validation confirms that the system is reliable, credible and will perform as expected. You should document how validation, testing, and re-validation is to be conducted. Modifications or additions made to the electronic system, such as software upgrades or data migration, can affect performance. These can, in turn, affect the quality of the validated applications, and thus the integrity of electronic information. The system’s reliability can also be questioned.

candidates.statement: For these reasons, you should assess and approve all changes, using your change control system, to hardware or software used in pharmacovigilance activities. This assessment will also help determine if re-validation is needed and the scope of re-validation.
